name.description: The task, in the words of the one who starts it: one line of 1 to 100 characters.

starts.description: Who or what starts it: a person, a clock, a message. One line of 1 to 200 characters.

ends.description: What is true at the end, with what makes it true. One line of 1 to 200 characters.

description.description: What it promises, what that costs, what must never happen, in 1 to 2,000 characters.

only.description: The condition under which the thing is there at all, begun with "when", "on" or "for", so that it reads after the word "only": `only: when a customer pays by card`. One line of at most 100 characters. Left out when it is always there.

feature.description: The id of the one feature the flow belongs to, a record in features/.

id.description: The step's own id in its flow, in the form of a record's id, given once. `flow#step` is its address.

does.description: The id of a connection (one part acts on another), of a part (it happens there) or of a flow (it runs here, whole). Never with `reply`.

reply.description: The id of an earlier step of this flow that names a connection, and not one that ends at a store: its answer travels back. An answer that comes back over several connections is a reply to each of their steps, the last first. Never with `does`.

after.description: The ids of earlier steps this one comes after, where that is not the step above. It comes after each of them that happens.

name.description: What happens, verb first: one line of 1 to 100 characters. Left out only where the name of the connection or of the flow in `does` says this step and no more. A reply always has one: it says what comes back. A step that happens once for each of several things says "each", as in `Weighs each tea of the order`. Where copies of one app take turns, it says which copy acts.

only.description: The condition under which the thing is there at all, begun with "when", "on" or "for", so that it reads after the word "only": `only: when a customer pays by card`. One line of at most 100 characters. Left out when it is always there.

description.description: A sentence or two of 1 to 300 characters: a wait, a retry, a refusal.

data.description: The ids of the data this step passes, records in data/: on a step on a connection, or on a reply. A list with no id twice. On a step that writes a store it names what the step puts there; on one that reads a store, what the store holds: what the reader makes of it is named on the step that puts it somewhere.

access.description: Whether this step reads or writes the store its connection ends at: `read` or `write`. Only on a step whose connection says `access: read-write`; left out there, the store shows nothing of the step's `data`. A step that reads one thing and writes another is two steps.

removes.description: The ids of the data that is no longer in the store after this step, records in data/, none twice: on a step on a connection that ends at a store. A read that takes a job off a queue names the job in `data` and in `removes`.

items.description: One step of a flow: what happens on a connection, in a part or as a whole flow, or the answer to an earlier step.

steps.description: The steps in order, at least one, each a mapping with its own `id`.

description: One path through the model, told for one outcome: what starts it, the acts in order, each on a record the model holds, and what is true at the end. It has one start and tells one way. Another way to the same outcome is a flow of its own; where the ways part for a few steps only, each of those steps has `only`, and the step at which they meet names the last step of each in `after`.
